parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is in the presentation layer, so it should only translate requests and responses and hand the work to the business layer. In PayrollController.submit it enforces a payroll rule itself: weekly hours must be between 0 and 80. It also throws the business error type PayrollRuleError when that check fails. The allowed range for weekly hours is a business invariant, not a check on the request's shape, so it belongs in the business (domain) layer, for example inside PayrollService.submitHours. Throwing a business rule error from the controller confirms the rule lives in the wrong layer. A weaker concern is that the controller decides when to write audit entries: it calls audit.log after both submit and approve. That is a business workflow policy, not presentation work. The export method only formats the business output through payslipRow, which is fine for presentation.

violations.message: PayrollController.submit enforces the payroll rule that weekly hours must be between 0 and 80 and throws PayrollRuleError. This rule belongs in the business (domain) layer, for example in PayrollService.submitHours, not in a presentation controller.

PayrollController.submit and approve decide when audit entries are written by calling audit.log after each payroll operation. This audit workflow is business policy and belongs in the business (domain) layer.
